verses.text: When David had gone a little past the top of the hill, Ziba, Mephibosheth's servant, came to meet him. He had a pair of donkeys with saddles on them, carrying two hundred loaves of bread, one hundred bunches of raisins, one hundred pieces of summer fruit, and a skin bag full of wine.

The king asked Ziba, "What are these for?" Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for the king's family to ride. The bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for anyone who becomes weak in the wilderness to drink."
The king asked, "Where is your master's grandson?" Ziba answered the king, "He is staying in Jerusalem. He said, 'Today the people of Israel will give me back my grandfather's kingdom.'"
Then the king said to Ziba, "Everything that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." Ziba said, "I bow down to you. May I always please you, my lord the king."
When King David came to Bahurim, a man from Saul's family came out of the town. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and he cursed David as he came out.
He threw stones at David and at all of King David's officials, even though all the people and the strong fighting men were on David's right and left.
As Shimei cursed, he said, "Get out, get out, you murderer, you wicked man!

The LORD is paying you back for all the blood of Saul's family. You took his place as king, and now the LORD has given the kingdom to your son Absalom. Look, you are ruined by your own evil, because you are a murderer!"
Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over there and cut off his head."
But the king said, "What has this got to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? If he is cursing me because the LORD told him, 'Curse David,' then who can ask him, 'Why are you doing this?'"

Then David said to Abishai and all his officials, "My own son, my own flesh and blood, is trying to kill me. So this man from Benjamin has even more reason to do this! Leave him alone and let him curse, because the LORD has told him to.
Perhaps the LORD will see the wrong being done to me and will give me good things in return for the cursing I receive today."
So David and his men kept going along the road. Shimei walked along the hillside across from him, cursing as he went, throwing stones at him and throwing dust in the air.
The king and all the people with him were very tired when they arrived, and he rested there.
Meanwhile, Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
Then David's friend Hushai the Arkite came to Absalom and said to him, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this how you show loyalty to your friend? Why didn't you go with your friend?"
Hushai said to Absalom, "No, I will belong to the one chosen by the LORD, by these people, and by all the men of Israel. I will stay with him.
Besides, who should I serve? Shouldn't I serve the son? Just as I served your father, so I will serve you."
Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give us your advice. What should we do?"

Ahithophel answered Absalom, "Sleep with your father's slave wives, the ones he left to take care of the palace. Then all Israel will hear that you have made yourself hateful to your father, and everyone who supports you will become even stronger."
So they set up a tent for Absalom on the roof of the palace, and Absalom slept with his father's slave wives where all Israel could see.
In those days, the advice Ahithophel gave was treated like a word from God himself. That is how both David and Absalom thought of all of Ahithophel's advice.
